title: introduce-sse-fragment-prioritizer-and-json-boundary-fence
author: Katherine Liu
description: Motivation: We continue to see client-side partial-JSON failures and out-of-order function_call events when fragments arrive interleaved or when delimiters are dropped under high-concurrency qps. This PR introduces a server-side SSE fragment prioritizer plus an explicit JSON boundary fence marker to make reconstruction deterministic for both OpenAI-compat and Redwood streaming consumers. Summary of changes: 1) fragment prioritizer: assigns intra-stream priority scores to fragments at enqueue time using a lightweight heuristic that prefers: (a) fragments containing structural tokens that open or close JSON objects/arrays, (b) fragments with function_call sentinels, (c) heartbeat/meta events (to preserve order guarantees). Prioritizer works with existing batching and keeps ordering guarantees for events that share the same logical sequence id. 2) json boundary fence: emit a small, explicit sentinel event ("redwood::json-fence:v1") at fence points where a complete JSON object/array boundary is observed by the runtime; fences are idempotent and ignored by clients that do not understand them. 3) reassembly changes: parser reassembly now recognizes the fence sentinel and uses it to resync partial-json heuristics, falling back to the previous checksum-based reassembly when fences are absent. 4) OpenAI-compat shim: compatibility layer maps fence events to a no-op for clients expecting only data/event messages but preserves function_call ordering semantics. 5) Telemetry and testing: adds histograms for fragment-priority distribution, counters for fence emissions, and an integration test harness that replays realistic interleaving under jitter. Backwards compatibility: fences are additive and optional; older clients simply ignore unknown event types. The prioritizer does not change logical sequence numbers and is constrained to operate within a watermark window to avoid starvation of low-priority fragments. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-3421) linked - [x] Unit tests for prioritizer heuristics - [x] Integration replay tests for partial-json recovery - [x] Console metrics dashboard tiles for fences/priority - [x] Feature-flag gate for early rollout Rollout plan: feature gated; enabled for 5% of hosted traffic for 48h, ramp to 25% if no regressions, then full rollout. Related: see ENG-3520 for long-term resharding work and SUP-9123 incident notes.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (2026-02-18): Nice approach. Two quick asks: add a test that simulates continuous low-priority stream starvation and ensure watermark advances; and add a short comment in the prioritizer code explaining why checksums are still required.

Katherine Liu (2026-02-19): Added starvation test and comments; prioritizer advances watermark using observed seq gaps so starvation window is bounded. See commit d4e5f6a and test file replay_starvation_test.rs.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-22): Can we avoid emitting fences for very small payloads (<24 bytes) to reduce noise? Also please ensure the OpenAI shim doesn't surface fence event types to clients.
Katherine Liu (2026-02-23): Fence emission now samples by payload size and keeps telemetry when sampled; shim explicitly drops fences for clients that do not opt-in. Updated openai_adapter.rs.
Samir Patel (2026-02-28): CI flake on integration replay fixed; LGTM pending minor doc clarifications.
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after approvals; small follow-up (post-merge) added to catch log verbosity under high throughput. No rollback required during 5% ramp. Monitoring dashboards show expected fence count and no increase in partial-json errors.
release_notes: Introduce server-side SSE fragment prioritizer and optional JSON boundary fence (redwood::json-fence:v1). This improves partial-JSON reconstruction and function_call event ordering under high-concurrency streaming. Backwards-compatible; clients that do not understand fence events will ignore them.
notes: Feature gated: runtime flag 'sse.fragment_prioritizer' controls activation.
Telemetry: metric sse.fence.emitted and sse.fragment.priority_histogram added.
Follow-up: ENG-3599 to evaluate heuristic tuning and reduce fence emission noise.
